messages:
amanda-plat: Heads up — Customer ACME (private VPC) reporting intermittent 403s to our KMS-backed key unwrap during model inference. Starts after ~10k tokens, seems to self-heal after ~30s. Customer says it's only from their private cluster behind their corporate DNS/proxy.
jorge-sre: Can you paste a short repro log snippet? 403 from KMS usually means auth or request mangling (headers/SNI).
amanda-plat: Pasted error from their pod logs:
amanda-plat: ```
2029-06-17T15:12:04Z inference: request id=xyz status=403 code=AccessDenied message="Access denied to KMS:Decrypt"
2029-06-17T15:12:04Z kms-client: tls handshake failure: handshake aborted
2029-06-17T15:12:34Z inference: request id=xyz status=200
``` 
sophie-sec: tls handshake failure + auth 403 suggests the proxy may be altering SNI or stripping a header used by our KMS signer. Do they use an on-path TLS-inspecting proxy? Ask whether they do explicit TLS termination.
amanda-plat: They confirmed: corporate web-proxy doing TLS interception (explicit) and a DNS-forwarder that rewrites upstream to internal proxy IPs. They also said the proxy sometimes injects a bypass for large requests but not consistently.
ops-rishi: If the proxy is doing MITM/TLS intercept it will present its own cert to clients and re-sign to upstream. Our KMS client validates KMS public key via certificate chain + SNI. If SNI is rewritten or cert CN doesn't match, the client might fail the handshake intermittently when the proxy chooses different upstreams.
jorge-sre: Request they test curl to the KMS endpoint from the same node:
jorge-sre: ```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://kms.api.prod.redwood.example/v1/unwrap
``` 
amanda-plat: They ran it. First attempt shows proxy cert chain and CN=corp-intercept.local, second attempt goes direct and CN=kms.api.prod.redwood.example. When direct it works. When intercepted: 403 in client because signing header X-Request-Id was stripped.
eng-bot: deploy-bot noted: No platform-side incidents. Dedicated/private infra healthy. This looks customer-side. Marking P2 until we confirm audit/log gaps.
sophie-sec: Two security/compliance concerns here we need to call out:
- Audit logs: customer's audit events for KMS Unwrap are only present for the successful calls; intercepted failures are not consistently logged because proxy rewrites request body/headers before we see them.
- Key material: if TLS is intercepted, customer-managed HSM/KMS expectations change — they must acknowledge MITM. Need to confirm they are allowed to perform TLS interception per their compliance.
amanda-plat: They asked why logs for the 403 attempts don't show up in our control plane audit logs (they need those for their SOC). We only see successful gRPC proxied requests; the intercepted failures never reach our KMS endpoints so nothing is logged.
ops-rishi: Repro steps for them (to run on one node):
1) Start a short looped inference request (token load).
2) Run tcpdump on node: `sudo tcpdump -nni eth0 host kms.api.prod.redwood.example and port 443 -w /tmp/kms.pcap`
3) When 403 occurs, capture `openssl s_client -connect kms.api.prod.redwood.example:443 -servername kms.api.prod.redwood.example -showcerts`
4) Export the HTTP headers with `mitm-proxy` disabled/enabled to compare.
amanda-plat: They returned pcap and openssl output showing the corporate proxy cert and SNI sometimes set to the proxy hostname. CCing their security lead.
sophie-sec: Mitigation options we recommend to customer:
- Configure their proxy to bypass KMS endpoints (allow direct egress to our KMS IPs/CNAMEs) — authoritative solution.
- If bypass impossible, configure proxy to preserve SNI and not strip x-custom-auth or X-Request-ID headers we rely on for auth telemetry.
- Ensure their TLS proxy uses a CA trusted by their clients only — but advise this is weaker for compliance than bypass.
jorge-sre: Temp workaround for customerspace: add a sidecar that tunnels KMS traffic over an outbound port that the proxy doesn't intercept (e.g., port 8443 to an external egress gateway). We'll share a sample stunnel config.
amanda-plat: Also flagged billing trace: some wraps failed and retried causing token overuse. Billing team please note potential token inflation during retries; customer wants credits for the retry storms.
eng-bot: billing-bot: filed #invoice-772 for credit review.
sophie-sec: Next steps assigned:
- amanda-plat: coordinate with customer on proxy bypass test (ETA 24h)
- jorge-sre: draft sidecar stunnel example + iptables SNAT rules (ETA 48h)
- ops-rishi: confirm list of KMS endpoints and IP ranges we can publish for allowlist (ETA 24h)
- sophie-sec: prepare a security advisory note re: TLS interception and audit log implications (ETA 72h)
amanda-plat: Customer accepted bypass test window tomorrow. I'll post results here. :thumbsup:
jorge-sre: sample iptables note for reference (for their ops):
jorge-sre: ```bash
# allow direct egress to KMS
iptables -t nat -A OUTPUT -p tcp -d 203.0.113.45 --dport 443 -j DNAT --to-destination 203.0.113.45:443
# SNAT via egress-gw
iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -p tcp -d 203.0.113.45 --dport 443 -j SNAT --to-source 198.51.100.10
```
amanda-plat: Thanks all — will update after the test. If proxy bypass works, we can close this as customer config issue; otherwise escalate to infra for deeper packet inspection.
summary: Intermittent KMS 403s in a Private VPC traced to corporate TLS-intercepting DNS/proxy that rewrites SNI/strips auth headers. Repro steps, mitigations, and action items captured.
